title: Zhou et al. (2022), AutoMorph
summary: AutoMorph combines quality assessment, anatomical segmentation and vascular measurements. It provides density, width, tortuosity and fractal descriptors from segmentation maps.
limits: Segmentation errors and imaging differences affect measurements. Literature associations do not establish a diagnosis or a threshold for this uploaded image.

title: Huang et al. (2021), Lesion-Based Contrastive Learning
summary: Lesion patches guide contrastive representation learning for DR grading. The released encoder produces image representations; a separate detector is needed for lesion boxes and counts.
limits: Embedding components do not correspond to named lesions. The authors separately warn about limited cross-dataset generalization of their lesion detector.

title: Selvaraju et al. (2017), Grad-CAM
summary: Grad-CAM weights convolutional activations using class-score gradients to localize regions contributing to a target prediction.
limits: It is coarse model attribution, not lesion segmentation, proof of causality or ground-truth localization. This implementation attributes only the fusion model image branch while holding tabular inputs fixed.

title: ADA (2022), International Clinical DR Disease Severity Scale
summary: The clinical scale defines five DR severity categories. Clinical findings are needed to establish a category.
limits: A model probability or weak feature map does not establish these clinical findings.

title: Retinal vascular geometry and 6-year incidence/progression of DR (2017)
summary: A longitudinal cohort examined tortuosity, branching, fractal dimension and caliber in relation to later DR outcomes. These descriptors can supply contextual vascular information beyond a grade alone.
limits: Observational associations do not identify causality, an individual risk probability or a normal range for this AutoMorph image.

title: Adebayo et al. (2018), Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
summary: Visual appeal alone does not establish that a saliency map faithfully explains a model. Model/data randomization checks can help evaluate an explanation method.
limits: This demo generates Grad-CAM but does not claim independent clinical or comprehensive saliency validation.

title: Huang et al., official lesion-detector documentation
summary: The project provides a lesion detector separately from its contrastive encoder and documents limits in cross-dataset detection performance.
limits: That separate detector checkpoint is not configured here. Unavailable detections are not equivalent to a negative lesion examination.
